name: 45-degree back extension
cue: Lower under control and rise until your body is in a straight line, without over-arching.

name: Banded lateral walk
cue: Keep tension on the band and push your knees out with each small side step.

name: Barbell back squat
cue: Sit down between your heels and drive up through your whole foot.

name: Barbell bench press
cue: Pin your shoulder blades back and lower the bar to mid-chest.

name: Barbell curl
cue: Keep your elbows at your sides and curl without swinging your body.
note: Hits both heads; a slightly wider grip may favour the short head, but evidence is limited.

name: Barbell hip thrust
cue: Tuck your chin, drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes hard at the top.

name: Barbell overhead press
cue: Squeeze your glutes and press the bar straight up, moving your head through at the top.

name: Barbell reverse curl
cue: Curl with an overhand grip and keep your wrists straight.

name: Barbell row
cue: Hinge to about 45 degrees and pull the bar to your lower ribs.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Barbell shrug
cue: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, then lower slowly.

name: Bayesian cable curl
cue: Face away from the cable and keep your arm slightly behind your body as you curl.
note: Arm behind the body stretches the long head; head-level evidence is limited.

name: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly
cue: Hinge forward and raise the dumbbells out wide without shrugging.

name: Bulgarian split squat
cue: Rest your back foot on the bench and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.

name: Cable crunch
cue: Kneel, hold the rope by your head and curl your ribs toward your hips.
note: Upper vs lower abs evidence is limited; the whole rectus abdominis works.

name: Cable hip abduction
cue: Stand tall and sweep the working leg out to the side without leaning.

name: Cable lateral raise
cue: Start with the cable across your body and raise your arm out to shoulder height.

name: Cable woodchop
cue: Rotate from your trunk, not your arms, moving the handle diagonally across your body.

name: Chest dip
cue: Lean your torso forward and let your elbows drift slightly out as you lower.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
cue: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and row with elbows out wide, squeezing your shoulder blades.

name: Chin-up
cue: Use a shoulder-width underhand grip and pull your elbows down to your sides.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Close-grip bench press
cue: Grip about shoulder-width, tuck your elbows and lower the bar to your lower chest.

name: Close-grip lat pulldown
cue: Use a close neutral grip and pull your elbows down toward your hips.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Cossack squat
cue: Shift into a deep squat over one leg while the other leg stays straight with toes up.

name: Crunch
cue: Curl your shoulders and ribs toward your hips while your lower back stays on the floor.
note: Upper vs lower abs evidence is limited; the whole rectus abdominis works.

name: Conventional deadlift
cue: Keep the bar against your legs, back flat, and push the floor away.

name: Decline barbell press
cue: Use a slight decline and lower the bar to the lower part of your chest.

name: Dumbbell bench press
cue: Lower the dumbbells to chest level for a deep stretch, then press up and slightly together.

name: Dumbbell triceps kickback
cue: Keep your upper arm still beside your torso and straighten the elbow fully.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
cue: Raise the dumbbells out to the side to shoulder height, leading with the elbows.

name: Dumbbell shrug
cue: Hold the dumbbells at your sides and lift your shoulders straight up, pausing at the top.

name: Dumbbell wrist curl
cue: Rest your forearms on a bench and curl the dumbbells up by bending at the wrist.

name: Face pull
cue: Pull the rope toward your face and split the ends so your hands finish beside your ears.

name: Front squat
cue: Keep your elbows high and your torso upright as you sit straight down.

name: Goblet squat
cue: Hold one dumbbell at your chest and sit down between your knees, chest up.

name: Hammer curl
cue: Curl with palms facing each other and elbows pinned to your sides.
note: Mostly brachialis and brachioradialis; the long-head label is a convention with limited evidence.

name: Hanging leg raise
cue: Hang still and curl your pelvis up as you raise your legs, without swinging.
note: Upper vs lower abs evidence is limited; the whole rectus abdominis works.

name: High-to-low cable fly
cue: Set the pulleys high and bring your hands down and together in front of your hips.

name: Incline barbell press
cue: Set the bench at about 30 degrees and lower the bar to your upper chest.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
cue: Sit back on an incline bench, let your arms hang behind you and curl without moving the elbows forward.
note: Arm behind the body stretches the long head; head-level evidence is limited.

name: Incline dumbbell press
cue: Set the bench at about 30 degrees and lower the dumbbells to your upper chest.

name: Kettlebell swing
cue: Snap your hips forward to float the bell to chest height; the arms just guide it.

name: Leg extension
cue: Sit back against the pad and fully straighten your knees, pausing at the top.

name: Leg press
cue: Lower until your knees are deeply bent while your lower back stays on the pad.

name: Low-to-high cable fly
cue: Set the pulleys low and sweep your hands up and together to upper-chest height.

name: Lying leg curl
cue: Keep your hips pressed into the pad and curl your heels toward your glutes.

name: Machine chest press
cue: Set the handles at mid-chest height and keep your shoulder blades against the pad.

name: Machine hip abduction
cue: Sit tall and push your knees out against the pads, controlling the way back.

name: Machine hip adduction
cue: Squeeze your legs together under control and let them open wide for a full stretch.

name: Machine preacher curl
cue: Keep the backs of your arms flat on the pad and lower all the way down slowly.
note: Arm in front of the body is thought to favour the short head; evidence is limited.

name: Machine shoulder press
cue: Keep your back on the pad and press up without locking out hard.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
cue: Hook your heels under a pad or have a partner hold them, then lower forward as slowly as you can, hips straight.

name: Overhead cable triceps extension
cue: Face away from the cable and let your hands travel behind your head for a deep stretch.

name: Overhead dumbbell triceps extension
cue: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands and lower it behind your head, elbows pointing up.

name: Pallof press
cue: Stand side-on to the cable and press the handle straight out without letting your body twist.

name: Pec deck fly
cue: Keep a slight bend in the elbows and squeeze your arms together in front of your chest.

name: Pull-up
cue: Grip a little wider than your shoulders and pull your chest toward the bar.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Push-up
cue: Keep a straight line from head to heels and lower your chest to just above the floor.

name: Reverse crunch
cue: Lie on your back and curl your hips off the floor toward your chest, then lower slowly.
note: Upper vs lower abs evidence is limited; the whole rectus abdominis works.

name: Reverse pec deck
cue: Face the pad and sweep your arms back wide, leading with the elbows.

name: Romanian deadlift
cue: Push your hips back with soft knees and lower the bar along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.

name: Seated cable row
cue: Sit tall and pull the handle to your stomach, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Seated calf raise
cue: Lower into a deep stretch, pause, then rise as high as you can.

name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
cue: Sit upright and press the dumbbells from ear height to just above your head.

name: Seated leg curl
cue: Lean your torso slightly forward to stretch the hamstrings and curl all the way down.

name: Single-arm cable row
cue: Drive the elbow toward your hip, not straight back.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Single-arm dumbbell row
cue: Brace on the bench and pull the dumbbell toward your hip in an arc.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Single-leg dumbbell calf raise
cue: Stand on a step on one foot and use the full range, from deep stretch to high on your toes.

name: Sissy squat
cue: Hold a support, rise onto your toes and lean back as your knees travel forward, hips straight.

name: Skull crusher
cue: Lower the bar behind your head rather than to your forehead, keeping your elbows pointed up.

name: Spider curl
cue: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with arms hanging straight and curl to the top.
note: Arm in front of the body is thought to favour the short head; evidence is limited.

name: Standing calf raise
cue: Keep your knees straight and pause in the deep stretch at the bottom.

name: Straight-arm pulldown
cue: With arms nearly straight, sweep the bar from eye level down to your thighs.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.

name: Sumo deadlift
cue: Take a wide stance, push your knees out and drive the floor apart as you stand.

name: Cable triceps pushdown
cue: Pin your elbows to your sides and push down until your arms are straight.

name: Walking lunge
cue: Take a long step and drop your back knee toward the floor, pushing through the front foot.

name: Wide-grip lat pulldown
cue: Grip wide and pull the bar to your upper chest, driving the elbows down and out.
note: Upper vs lower lat emphasis is a coaching convention; evidence is limited.
